scenes.tts: Culture shows how the program runs. What happens in a whole animal when you delete its parts?
scenes.visual: Title card: Take the Machinery Away. A mouse silhouette beside the pathway diagram.
scenes.narration: Culture shows how the program runs. What happens in a whole animal when you delete its parts?

scenes.tts: Delete caspase three, or caspase nine, from a mouse. Do the spinal and peripheral neurons that normally die survive?
scenes.caption: Delete caspase-3, or caspase-9, from a mouse. Do the spinal and peripheral neurons that normally die survive?
scenes.visual: Question card held. A knockout mouse: caspase-3 or caspase-9 crossed out on its chromosome and in the pathway diagram.
scenes.narration: Delete caspase-3, or caspase-9, from a mouse. Do the spinal and peripheral neurons that normally die survive?

scenes.tts: No. Oppenheim's group counted them. The same number died as in normal mice.
scenes.visual: Bar chart: neuron deaths, normal mouse versus caspase-null mouse, equal bars.
scenes.narration: No. Oppenheim's group counted them. The same number died as in normal mice.

scenes.tts: But the deaths came later, and they did not look apoptotic.
scenes.visual: Timeline: the caspase-null deaths shifted later.
scenes.narration: But the deaths came later, and they did not look apoptotic.

scenes.tts: Chromatin condensation was absent or reduced. The cytoplasm filled with vacuoles.
scenes.visual: Side by side: a pyknotic apoptotic neuron, and a caspase-null neuron full of vacuoles.
scenes.narration: Chromatin condensation was absent or reduced. The cytoplasm filled with vacuoles.

scenes.tts: So deleting a caspase changes how these neurons die.
scenes.visual: Label: caspases decide how.
scenes.narration: So deleting a caspase changes how these neurons die.

scenes.tts: Now delete Bax instead. In many neuron populations, naturally occurring death was largely eliminated.
scenes.visual: Bax crossed out. A ganglion that stays crowded with neurons. On screen: rescued populations include sympathetic and sensory neurons, facial motor neurons, retinal ganglion cells.
scenes.narration: Now delete Bax instead. In many neuron populations, naturally occurring death was largely eliminated.

scenes.tts: Bax deletion does not rescue every developing neuron. But where neurons depend on Bax, deleting it stops the death.
scenes.visual: Caveat note: not every population. Label: in Bax-dependent populations.
scenes.narration: Bax deletion does not rescue every developing neuron. But where neurons depend on Bax, deleting it stops the death.

scenes.tts: In those populations, caspases decide how. Bax decides whether.
scenes.visual: Two-line card: caspases decide how; Bax decides whether. Small label: in Bax-dependent populations.
scenes.narration: In those populations, caspases decide how. Bax decides whether.

scenes.tts: The saved neurons were not normal.
scenes.visual: Close-up of the surplus neurons.
scenes.narration: The saved neurons were not normal.

scenes.tts: In the spinal nerve roots and the facial nerve, myelinated axon counts rose by about thirty to fifty-five percent. Many extra axons were very small.
scenes.visual: Three cross-sections, dorsal root, ventral root and facial nerve: more myelinated axons, many very small. On screen: about 31, 53 and 54 percent more than normal mice.
scenes.narration: In the spinal nerve roots and the facial nerve, myelinated axon counts rose by about 30 to 55 percent. Many extra axons were very small.
scenes.caption: In the spinal nerve roots and the facial nerve, myelinated axon counts rose by about 30 to 55 percent. Many extra axons were very small.

scenes.tts: Extra spinal motor neurons began to innervate their targets. Then a subset shrank, and lost contact.
scenes.visual: Motor axons reach a muscle; some neurons then shrink and their axons pull away.
scenes.narration: Extra spinal motor neurons began to innervate their targets. Then a subset shrank, and lost contact.

scenes.tts: A neuron saved from death may survive as a smaller cell. That fits too little target support.
scenes.visual: Label: alive, but small; limited target support?
scenes.narration: A neuron saved from death may survive as a smaller cell. That fits too little target support.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking N G F lose their sympathetic neurons. So you cannot ask what else N G F does for them.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking NGF lose their sympathetic neurons. So you cannot ask what else NGF does for them.
scenes.visual: NGF-null mouse: the sympathetic ganglion empties.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking NGF lose their sympathetic neurons. So you cannot ask what else NGF does for them.

scenes.tts: In mice lacking both N G F and Bax, the sympathetic neurons survive.
scenes.caption: In mice lacking both NGF and Bax, the sympathetic neurons survive.
scenes.visual: NGF and Bax both crossed out: the ganglion stays full.
scenes.narration: In mice lacking both NGF and Bax, the sympathetic neurons survive.

scenes.tts: If N G F did nothing but keep neurons alive, what would their innervation of organs look like?
scenes.caption: If NGF did nothing but keep neurons alive, what would their innervation of organs look like?
scenes.visual: Question card held over an organ map: salivary gland, heart, stomach, kidney, trachea.
scenes.narration: If NGF did nothing but keep neurons alive, what would their innervation of organs look like?

scenes.tts: It would look like the innervation in mice lacking only Bax. It did not.
scenes.visual: The organ map begins to colour. Label: double nulls compared with Bax-null mice, embryos and newborns.
scenes.narration: It would look like the innervation in mice lacking only Bax. It did not.

scenes.tts: The axons failed to fully innervate many targets, and the failure differed by organ.
scenes.visual: Organ map coloured by innervation: absent, greatly reduced, somewhat reduced, normal.
scenes.narration: The axons failed to fully innervate many targets, and the failure differed by organ.

scenes.tts: The salivary glands had none, or almost none. The heart was greatly reduced. The trachea was normal.
scenes.visual: Salivary glands marked absent or nearly absent; heart greatly reduced; stomach and kidneys somewhat reduced; trachea normal.
scenes.narration: The salivary glands had none, or almost none. The heart was greatly reduced. The trachea was normal.

scenes.tts: So N G F is needed for axons to grow into many targets, as well as for survival.
scenes.caption: So NGF is needed for axons to grow into many targets, as well as for survival.
scenes.visual: Card: NGF for survival, and for growing into targets.
scenes.narration: So NGF is needed for axons to grow into many targets, as well as for survival.

scenes.tts: Here is the general logic. Delete the death machinery, and look at what is still wrong once dying is no longer an option.
scenes.visual: Logic card: delete the machinery, then see what is still wrong.
scenes.narration: Here is the general logic. Delete the death machinery, and look at what is still wrong once dying is no longer an option.

scenes.tts: The deleted gene may have other jobs too, so read such results with care.
scenes.visual: Caveat note: the deleted gene may have other jobs.
scenes.narration: The deleted gene may have other jobs too, so read such results with care.

scenes.tts: The killers are already built; a survival signal keeps brakes on them.
scenes.visual: Line 1 appears.
scenes.narration: The killers are already built; a survival signal keeps brakes on them.

scenes.tts: Brake one is the gate at the mitochondrion. N G F loss opens it through new gene expression.
scenes.visual: Line 2 appears.
scenes.narration: Brake one is the gate at the mitochondrion. NGF loss opens it through new gene expression.
scenes.caption: Brake one is the gate at the mitochondrion. NGF loss opens it through new gene expression.

scenes.tts: Brake two is on the caspases, and deprivation lifts it without new protein.
scenes.visual: Line 3 appears.
scenes.narration: Brake two is on the caspases, and deprivation lifts it without new protein.

scenes.tts: The neuron dies by apoptosis only when both brakes are off.
scenes.visual: Line 4 appears.
scenes.narration: The neuron dies by apoptosis only when both brakes are off.

scenes.tts: Which neurons get enough N G F in the first place is a question about targets, and about competition.
scenes.caption: Which neurons get enough NGF in the first place is a question about targets, and about competition.
scenes.visual: End card line: the killers are built; NGF keeps two brakes on them.
scenes.narration: Which neurons get enough NGF in the first place is a question about targets, and about competition.
